newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed - Mogas up $1.50 but CFDs eas.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed - Mogas up $1.50 but CFDs eas.

text.p: European oil swaps ended mixed on Friday with gasoline firm, fuel flat and Brent CFDs slightly easier.
Gasoline climbed $1.50 a tonne but was 50 cents off the day's highs at $196.50 for May with June $3 lower.
Gasoline crack spreads against Brent held steady at $4.10 a barrel (3Q97), $3.10 (4Q97) and $3.50 (1Q98).
Dealers said the market still lacked demand from the U.S. ahead of the summer driving season.
Heavy fuel swaps were broadly unchanged after falling back from a firmer start to the day.
May barges traded up to $84.50 before sliding to trade at $83 a couple of times at the close. June traded 50 cents higher with July a further 75 cents above June.
Low sulphur swaps were quiet with May done at $87.75 a tonne and July pegged around $89.25.
Brent CFDs slipped about five cents lower for next week and the contango between next week and the week after was re-established after being erased on Thursday.
The next three were valued at 38 cents, 36 cents and 36 cents under June respectively.
Gas oil was little changed with spreads against Brent crude holding at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98).
Premiums for physical was well bid with trade at $12.50 a tonne above the IPE for May diesel (0.05 pct sulphur). June was pegged about $2 lower at $11.50 over.

Jet premiums were flat with May bid at $24.50 a tonne above the IPE after trading at that level last Thursday. The third and fourth quarters were little changed at $27.50 and $31.50 above the screen respectively.
